findings.title: Success path unconditionally forces CLOSED, discarding concurrent opens
findings.evidence: After the try block the success path runs 'with self._lock:' and then resets state/failures/opened_at/probe_in_flight to the closed defaults even though 'probing' was captured at admission time.
findings.recommendation: Record the state (or a generation counter) at admission and only clear failures / close the circuit if the breaker is still in that same generation; if the state changed to OPEN while the call was in flight, leave the breaker OPEN (and do not touch _opened_at). Same guard applies to the CLOSED-failure branch, which currently bumps _opened_at and extends the cooldown for calls admitted before the open.

findings.title: A hung half-open probe wedges the breaker open forever
findings.evidence: Once a probe is admitted with 'self._probe_in_flight = True', only the probe returning (success, Exception, or BaseException) clears the flag; there is no timeout and any later caller gets CircuitOpenError('half-open probe in flight') indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Stamp the probe admission time and let _refresh_locked re-admit (or re-open) when the probe exceeds a configurable probe timeout, or document that callers must supply their own timeout.

findings.title: No tests added for the state machine or its concurrency guarantees
findings.evidence: The change adds only the breaker module; the diff contains no tests for open/half-open transitions, the single-probe rejection path, or concurrent call/failure interleavings, and no test commands were run.
findings.recommendation: Add tests using an injected fake clock for CLOSED->OPEN, OPEN->HALF_OPEN after reset_timeout, probe success/failure, rejection while a probe is in flight, and at least one multi-threaded interleaving covering a slow success racing concurrent failures.
